definitions.explanation: A distinct section of a piece of writing, usually dealing with a single theme or idea.

definitions.gloss: end of a phase; conclusion of a stage
definitions.explanation: A natural stopping point or conclusion of a process or task. Often used in the expression {一段落|いちだんらく} to mean reaching a point where one can pause.

examples.japanese: {次|つぎ}の{段落|だんらく}を{読|よ}んでください。
この{文章|ぶんしょう}は{三|みっ}つの{段落|だんらく}に{分|わ}かれている。
examples.english: This passage is divided into three paragraphs.

examples.japanese: {作文|さくぶん}を{書|か}くときは{段落|だんらく}の{分|わ}け{方|かた}に{注意|ちゅうい}しましょう。
examples.english: When writing an essay, pay attention to how you divide paragraphs.

examples.japanese: {仕事|しごと}が{一段落|いちだんらく}した。
examples.english: The work has reached a stopping point.

examples.japanese: {引|ひ}っ{越|こ}しの{準備|じゅんび}がやっと{一段落|いちだんらく}ついた。
examples.english: The preparations for moving have finally settled down.

examples.japanese: {忙|いそが}しい{時期|じき}が{一段落|いちだんらく}したら、{旅行|りょこう}に{行|い}きたい。
examples.english: Once the busy period wraps up, I want to go on a trip.

notes:
Has two distinct uses: as a writing term for paragraph, and in the compound {一段落|いちだんらく} meaning the end of a phase.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {段落|だんらく}を{分|わ}ける (to divide into paragraphs)
- {一段落|いちだんらく}つく (to reach a stopping point)
- {一段落|いちだんらく}する (to settle down, to wrap up a phase)

READING NOTE:
The compound {一段落|いちだんらく} is traditionally read いちだんらく, though the reading ひとだんらく is also widely used in spoken Japanese.
